e-491.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
e-491.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int uv' \, \textrm{d}x= uv - \int vu' \, \textrm{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\displaystyle  \int xe^{7x} \textrm{d}x$ as $\displaystyle  \int uv'\,\textrm{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{7x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}-\int \frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{7}\int {e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{7}(\frac{{e}^{7x}}{7})+C \\  & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{49}{e}^{7x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

e-492.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
e-492.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int uv'\,\textrm{d}x= uv- \int vu'\,\textrm{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\displaystyle \int x \cos{2x} \textrm{d}x$ as $\displaystyle \int uv'\,\textrm{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\int \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+C\end{aligned}
$$

e-6209.knowledge_point: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts
e-6209.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x) & ⟹\,v=-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =-x\cdot \frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)-\int (-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x))\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =-{\frac{1}{5}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)|}_{0}^{\pi /5}+\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\frac{1}{5}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)|}_{0}^{\pi /5}+{\frac{1}{5}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5})|}_{0}^{\pi /5} \\  & =[-\frac{1}{5}\cdot \frac{\pi }{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+\frac{1}{5}\cdot 0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0)]+[\frac{1}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\frac{1}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)] \\  & =[-\frac{\pi }{25}\cdot (-1)+0]+[0-0] \\  & =\frac{\pi }{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=x and dv=e^{-3x}dx gives v=-e^{-3x}/3. Thus the integral is -xe^{-3x}/3+(1/3)∫e^{-3x}dx=-xe^{-3x}/3-e^{-3x}/9+C, matching option a.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x{e}^{-3x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-3x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{x{e}^{-3x}}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{x{e}^{-3x}}{3}-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{9}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Calculate the integral ∫xe−3xdx.

a
−xe−3x3−e−3x9+C
b
−xe3x3+e3x9+C
c
e−3x3−xe−3x9+C
d
xe−3x9+e−3x9+C
e
xe−3x9−e−3x3+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫xe−3xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=x⟹u′=1v′=e−3x⟹v=−e−3x3.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫x⋅e−3xdx=x⋅(−e−3x3)−∫(−e−3x3)⋅1dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫xe−3xdx=−xe−3x3+13∫e−3xdx=−xe−3x3−e−3x9+C

content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x{e}^{-3x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-3x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{x{e}^{-3x}}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{x{e}^{-3x}}{3}-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{9}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Calculate ∫6xe−3xdx.

a
 −xe−3x+2e−3x3+C
b
 −2xe−3x−2e−3x3+C
c
 4xe−3x−3e−3x2+C
d
 xe−3x2−2e−3x3+C
e
 −3xe−3x−e−3x3+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Using integration by parts with u=6x and dv=e^{-3x}dx gives du=6dx and v=-e^{-3x}/3. Therefore the integral is -2xe^{-3x}+2∫e^{-3x}dx=-2xe^{-3x}-(2/3)e^{-3x}+C, matching option b.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 6x{e}^{-3x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-3x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We, substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 6x\cdot {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =6x\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})\cdot 6\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2x{e}^{-3x}+2\int {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6x{e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =-2x{e}^{-3x}+2\int {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2x{e}^{-3x}-\frac{2{e}^{-3x}}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Calculate ∫6xe−3xdx.

a
 −xe−3x+2e−3x3+C
b
 −2xe−3x−2e−3x3+C
c
 4xe−3x−3e−3x2+C
d
 xe−3x2−2e−3x3+C
e
 −3xe−3x−e−3x3+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫6xe−3xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=6x⟹u′=6v′=e−3x⟹v=−e−3x3.

We, substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫6x⋅e−3xdx=6x⋅(−e−3x3)−∫(−e−3x3)⋅6dx=−2xe−3x+2∫e−3xdx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫6xe−3xdx=−2xe−3x+2∫e−3xdx=−2xe−3x−2e−3x3+C

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option b. Differentiating -2xe^{-3x}-(2/3)e^{-3x}+C gives -2e^{-3x}+6xe^{-3x}+2e^{-3x}=6xe^{-3x}. The deliberately submitted option e is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 6x{e}^{-3x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-3x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We, substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 6x\cdot {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =6x\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})\cdot 6\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2x{e}^{-3x}+2\int {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6x{e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =-2x{e}^{-3x}+2\int {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2x{e}^{-3x}-\frac{2{e}^{-3x}}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 3
?

Calculate the integral ∫3xe−xdx.

a
−3xe−x+e−x+C
b
−3xe−x−2e−x+C
c
2e−x−3xe−x+C
d
−3xe−x−3e−x+C
e
3e−x−xe−x+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=3x and dv=e^{-x}dx gives du=3dx and v=-e^{-x}. Thus ∫3xe^{-x}dx=-3xe^{-x}+3∫e^{-x}dx=-3xe^{-x}-3e^{-x}+C, matching option d.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x{e}^{-x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-x}\, & ⟹\,v=-{e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (-{e}^{-x})-\int (-{e}^{-x})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =-3x{e}^{-x}+3\int {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3x{e}^{-x}-3{e}^{-x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Calculate the integral ∫3xe−xdx.

a
−3xe−x+e−x+C
b
−3xe−x−2e−x+C
c
2e−x−3xe−x+C
d
−3xe−x−3e−x+C
e
3e−x−xe−x+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫3xe−xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=3x⟹u′=3v′=e−x⟹v=−e−x.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get ∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫3x⋅e−xdx=3x⋅(−e−x)−∫(−e−x)⋅3dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫3xe−xdx=−3xe−x+3∫e−xdx=−3xe−x−3e−x+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x{e}^{-x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-x}\, & ⟹\,v=-{e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (-{e}^{-x})-\int (-{e}^{-x})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =-3x{e}^{-x}+3\int {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3x{e}^{-x}-3{e}^{-x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 4
?

Calculate ∫x3xdx.

a
 3xln⁡3(x−1ln⁡3)+C
b
 3xln⁡3(1ln⁡3−x2)+C
c
 3xln⁡3(x−13)+C
d
 3xln⁡3(2x+1ln⁡3)+C
e
 3xln⁡3(x−1)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=x and dv=3^x dx gives v=3^x/ln(3). Therefore the integral is x3^x/ln(3)-3^x/(ln(3))^2+C, which factors into option a.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x{3}^{x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′} & ={3}^{x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {3}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\int \frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{3}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{x{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\int \frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{{3}^{x}}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)^{2}}+C \\  & =\frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(x-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3})+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Calculate ∫x3xdx.

a
 3xln⁡3(x−1ln⁡3)+C
b
 3xln⁡3(1ln⁡3−x2)+C
c
 3xln⁡3(x−13)+C
d
 3xln⁡3(2x+1ln⁡3)+C
e
 3xln⁡3(x−1)+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫x3xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=x⟹u′=1v′=3x⟹v=3xln⁡3.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫x⋅3xdx=x⋅3xln⁡3−∫3xln⁡3⋅1dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫x3xdx=x3xln⁡3−∫3xln⁡3dx=x3xln⁡3−3x(ln⁡3)2+C=3xln⁡3(x−1ln⁡3)+C

verification.explanation: The revealed integration-by-parts solution confirms option a: x3^x/ln(3)-3^x/(ln(3))^2+C. Differentiation gives x3^x, since the extra 3^x/ln(3) terms cancel. Option e was deliberately submitted incorrectly.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x{3}^{x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′} & ={3}^{x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {3}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\int \frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{3}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{x{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\int \frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{{3}^{x}}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)^{2}}+C \\  & =\frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(x-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3})+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5

∫x5xdx=

a
5xln⁡5(x−1ln⁡5)+C
b
5xln⁡5(x+1ln⁡5)+C
c
5xln⁡5(x−1)+C
d
5xln⁡5(1x−xln⁡5)+C
e
5xln⁡5(1−xln⁡5)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=x and dv=5^x dx gives v=5^x/ln(5). Hence the integral is x5^x/ln(5)-5^x/(ln(5))^2+C, which factors into option a.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x{5}^{x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={5}^{x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {5}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}-\int \frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{5}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{x{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}-\int \frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}-\frac{{5}^{x}}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5))^{2}}+C \\  & =\frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(x-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5})+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=x and dv=cos(5x)dx gives v=sin(5x)/5. Thus the integral is x sin(5x)/5−(1/5)∫sin(5x)dx=x sin(5x)/5+cos(5x)/25+C, matching option b.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$

a
 xsin⁡(5x)15+cos⁡(5x)5+C
b
xsin⁡(5x)5+cos⁡(5x)25+C
c

d

e
 2sin⁡(5x)5−xcos⁡(5x)15+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫xcos⁡(5x)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=x⟹u′=1v′=cos⁡(5x)⟹v=sin⁡(5x)5.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫x⋅cos⁡(5x)dx=x⋅(sin⁡(5x)5)−∫(sin⁡(5x)5)⋅1dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫xcos⁡(5x)dx=xsin⁡(5x)5−15∫sin⁡(5x)dx=xsin⁡(5x)5+cos⁡(5x)25+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$

We need to express $\int 3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫3xcos⁡(3x)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=3x⟹u′=3v′=cos⁡(3x)⟹v=sin⁡(3x)3.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫3x⋅cos⁡(3x)dx=3x⋅(sin⁡(3x)3)−∫(sin⁡(3x)3)⋅3dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫3xcos⁡(3x)dx=xsin⁡(3x)−∫sin⁡(3x)dx=xsin⁡(3x)+cos⁡(3x)3+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=5x and dv=sin(x)dx gives v=−cos(x). Thus the integral is −5x cos(x)+5∫cos(x)dx=−5x cos(x)+5sin(x)+C, matching option b.

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=5 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 5x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =5x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 5\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Calculate ∫5xsin⁡(x)dx.

a
cos⁡5x+xsin⁡5x+C
b
−5xcos⁡x+5sin⁡x+C
c
−xcos⁡x−cos⁡5x+C
d
−5xsin⁡x+cos⁡x+C
e
5xcos⁡x−xsin⁡x+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫5xsin⁡(x)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=5x⟹u′=5v′=sin⁡(x)⟹v=−cos⁡(x).

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫5x⋅sin⁡(x)dx=5x⋅(−cos⁡(x))−∫(−cos⁡(x))⋅5dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫5xsin⁡(x)dx=−5xcos⁡(x)+5∫cos⁡(x)dx=−5xcos⁡(x)+5sin⁡(x)+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=5 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 5x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =5x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 5\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=2x and dv=sin(x)dx gives v=−cos(x). Thus the integral is −2x cos(x)+2∫cos(x)dx=−2x cos(x)+2sin(x)+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Calculate ∫2xsin⁡(x)dx.

a
−xcos⁡x−cos⁡2x+C
b
2xcos⁡x−xsin⁡x+C
c
−2xsin⁡x+cos⁡x+C
d
cos⁡2x+xsin⁡2x+C
e
−2xcos⁡x+2sin⁡x+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫2xsin⁡(x)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=2x⟹u′=2v′=sin⁡(x)⟹v=−cos⁡(x).

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫2x⋅sin⁡(x)dx=2x⋅(−cos⁡(x))−∫(−cos⁡(x))⋅2dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫2xsin⁡(x)dx=−2xcos⁡(x)+2∫cos⁡(x)dx=−2xcos⁡(x)+2sin⁡(x)+C

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option e. Differentiating −2x cos(x)+2sin(x)+C gives −2cos(x)+2x sin(x)+2cos(x)=2x sin(x).

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 10
?

Calculate ∫2xcos⁡4xdx.

a
 xsin⁡4x2+cos⁡4x8+C
b
 −sin⁡4x4+xcos⁡4x6+C
c
 xsin⁡4x4−cos⁡4x2+C
d
 −sin⁡4x8+xcos⁡4x2+C
e
 3xsin⁡4x2+cos⁡4x4+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=2x and dv=cos(4x)dx gives v=sin(4x)/4. Thus the integral is x sin(4x)/2−(1/2)∫sin(4x)dx=x sin(4x)/2+cos(4x)/8+C, matching option a.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\int \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡4x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x)+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Calculate ∫2xcos⁡4xdx.

a
 xsin⁡4x2+cos⁡4x8+C
b
 −sin⁡4x4+xcos⁡4x6+C
c
 xsin⁡4x4−cos⁡4x2+C
d
 −sin⁡4x8+xcos⁡4x2+C
e
 3xsin⁡4x2+cos⁡4x4+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫2xcos⁡4xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=2x⟹u′=2v′=cos⁡4x⟹v=14sin⁡4x.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫2xcos⁡4xdx=2x⋅14sin⁡4x−∫14sin⁡4x⋅2dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫2xcos⁡4xdx=12xsin⁡4x−12∫sin⁡4xdx=12xsin⁡4x−12(−14cos⁡4x)+C=12xsin⁡4x+18cos⁡4x+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\int \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡4x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x)+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts gives the antiderivative −x cos(x)+sin(x). Its value at π/2 is 1 and at π/6 is −√3π/12+1/2. Subtracting gives √3π/12+1/2, matching option a.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}+{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-[\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\frac{\pi }{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})] \\  & +[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})] \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot 0-\frac{\pi }{6}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}]+[1-\frac{1}{2}] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\pi }{12}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11

Evaluate ∫π/6π/2xsin⁡xdx.

a
3π12+12
b
2π6−12
c
2π12+12
d
3π12+1
e
3π6−12
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's use integration by parts. We set

u=x⟹u′=1v′=sin⁡x⟹v=−cos⁡x.

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫x⋅sin⁡xdx=−x⋅cos⁡x−∫(−cos⁡x)⋅1dx.

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

∫xsin⁡xdx=−xcos⁡x|π/6π/2+∫π/6π/2cos⁡xdx=−xcos⁡x|π/6π/2+sin⁡x|π/6π/2=−[π2cos⁡(π2)−π6cos⁡(π6)]=+[sin⁡(π2)−sin⁡(π6)]=[π2⋅0−π6⋅32]+[1−12]=3π12+12.

content.knowledge_point: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts
content.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}+{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-[\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\frac{\pi }{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})] \\  & +[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})] \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot 0-\frac{\pi }{6}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}]+[1-\frac{1}{2}] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\pi }{12}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{3x} & ⇒ & v=\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot \frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}-\int (\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/3}2x{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & ={\frac{2}{3}x{e}^{3x}|}_{0}^{1/3}-\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1/3}{e}^{3x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{2}{3}x{e}^{3x}|}_{0}^{1/3}-{\frac{2}{9}{e}^{3x}|}_{0}^{1/3} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}[\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3(1/3)}-0\cdot {e}^{3\cdot 0}]-\frac{2}{9}[{e}^{3(1/3)}-{e}^{3\cdot 0}] \\  & =\frac{2}{3}[\frac{e}{3}-0]-\frac{2}{9}[e-1] \\  & =\frac{2e}{9}-\frac{2e}{9}+\frac{2}{9} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=5 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x) & ⇒ & v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 5x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =5x\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}-\int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}\cdot 5\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x){|}_{0}^{\pi /5}-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x){|}_{0}^{\pi /5}+\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x){|}_{0}^{\pi /5} \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\cdot \frac{\pi }{5})-0\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\cdot 0)] \\  & +\frac{1}{5}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\cdot \frac{\pi }{5})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\cdot 0)] \\  & =(0-0)+\frac{1}{5}(-1-1) \\  & =-\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
